title: Start-up failure is always visible, and a private GitHub email still gives the member's email
seam: src/main/app/ and src/main/features/tools/, plus the guidance line on src/renderer/screens/setup-check/
story: If Grillo hits an error while starting, it now shows the reason in an error dialog and closes; before, it opened no window and left a hidden process only Task Manager could end. On the Setup screen, a member who keeps their GitHub email private is told to approve the one-time email permission in the browser, and pressing Check again then shows their email. Sign-in itself is unchanged (gh auth login --web).

checks.criterion: A feature whose register() throws at start-up makes Grillo show the error in the system's error dialog and then quit.
checks.steps: Add a made-up feature folder src/main/features/zz-broken/ipc.ts whose register() throws new Error('made-up failure'). Run npm run dev. Press OK on the dialog. Remove the folder.
checks.expected: A dialog headed 'Grillo could not start', then "Feature 'zz-broken' could not start: made-up failure", then 'Grillo will close now…'. After OK, no Grillo or electron process is left running.

checks.criterion: When the member's email comes back empty, the setup check shows the scope command; after it runs the email is read again.
checks.steps: Sign in a made-up GitHub account that keeps its email private and lacks the user:email scope with gh auth login --web. Open Grillo on the Setup tab. Run gh auth refresh -h github.com -s user:email and approve it in the browser. Press Check again.
checks.expected: Before: Email reads 'Not shared yet', the refresh command shows with '…approve it in your browser, then press Check again.', and Check again and Continue are enabled. After Check again: the primary email shows and the step is gone.
